definitions.explanation: The act of being forced to leave a building or land, typically by legal or official order.

examples.japanese: {立|た}ち{退|の}きを{命|めい}じられた。
{住民|じゅうみん}は{立|た}ち{退|の}きに{反対|はんたい}している。
examples.english: The residents are opposing the eviction.

examples.japanese: {再開発|さいかいはつ}のため、このビルの{住民|じゅうみん}は{来月|らいげつ}までに{立|た}ち{退|の}きを{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: Due to redevelopment, the residents of this building are being asked to vacate by next month.

notes: Derived from the verb {立|た}ち{退|の}く (to vacate, to move out). Common collocations include {立|た}ち{退|の}きを{命|めい}じる (to order an eviction), {立|た}ち{退|の}き{料|りょう} (eviction compensation money), {立|た}ち{退|の}き{要求|ようきゅう} (eviction demand), and {強制|きょうせい}{立|た}ち{退|の}き (forced eviction). Often appears in news about urban redevelopment and landlord-tenant disputes.
